ITQAN:v2p373/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p373/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p373/r10.claim: حبا جما means abundant or much; Umayya’s poem illustrates the usage.
ITQAN:v2p373/r10.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ حبا جما ﴾ قال كثيرا أما سمعت قول أمية

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.claim: Favours and deprivation test whether people become grateful and fulfill others' rights or grow conceited, and whether they remain content or despair; the peaceful soul succeeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.anchor: He is testing whether blessing someone with favours makes him grateful

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r3.claim: Prosperity tests gratitude and care for others rather than pride and usurpation; hardship tests contentment rather than despair, and people should examine their treatment of orphans and the poor.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r3.anchor: with the orphans and the poor after receiving

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p312/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p312/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p312/r2.claim: Obsessive love of wealth blinds people to humanitarianism, decency, justice, and compassion, leaving higher values no place in their hearts.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p312/r2.anchor: The lust for wealth has made them blind to everything else and made them indifferent to the values of humanitarianism, decency, justice and compassion.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p422/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p422/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p422/r3.claim: They love money greatly and are eager to amass it; جمّ means abundant, as with water gathered in a pool.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p422/r3.anchor: أي كثيرا، يعني: تحبون جمع المال وتولعون به، يقال: جم الماء في الحوض، إذا كثر واجتمع.

BAYDAWI-FULL:89:20-25/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:20-25/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:20-25/r1.claim: They love wealth excessively, with greed and avarice; Abū ʿAmr, Sahl, and Yaʿqūb read the surrounding verbs from لا يكرمون through ويحبون in third person.
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:20-25/r1.anchor: { وتحبون المال حبا جما } كثيرا مع حرص وشره، وقرأ أبو عمرو وسهل ويعقوب

NAHHAS:v5p223/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p223/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p223/r5.claim: Kallā is a rebuke throughout the Qurʾān: people should not behave this way and should desist.
NAHHAS:v5p223/r5.anchor: تماما في كل القرآن قال المعنى لا ينبغي أن يكونوا هكذا وانزجروا عن هذا الفعل

DURR-FULL:v8p511/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p511/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v8p511/r2.claim: He heard the Prophet read four clauses in the third person plural: they do not honor or urge feeding, consume inheritance greedily, and love wealth intensely.
DURR-FULL:v8p511/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه

DURR-FULL:v8p511/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p511/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v8p511/r3.claim: He reports that the Prophet read the clauses about honoring the orphan, feeding the poor, and loving wealth with third-person plural forms.
DURR-FULL:v8p511/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p325/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p325/r1.speaker: طرفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p325/r1.claim: Tarafa's lines voice the pre-Islamic boast that wealth, noble children, and status reflect divine favor and rank.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p325/r1.anchor: قال طرفة : فلو شاء ربي كنت قيس بن عاصم ولو شاء ربي كنت عمرو بن مرثد

ZAJJAJ:v5p323/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p323/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p323/r1.claim: Jamman means abundant; turāth derives from wirāth, with tāʾ replacing wāw when the wāw is ḍamma, as in wijāh becoming tijāh.
ZAJJAJ:v5p323/r1.anchor: ولكن التاء تبدل من الواو إذا كانت الواو مضمومة،

TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r15.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r15.claim: They explain “jamma” as abundant, intense love of wealth that makes people hoard rather than spend for good.
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r15.anchor: أي كثيرا شديدا عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r16.claim: Another view says greedy people gather wealth by any means and spend it badly without considering consequences.
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r16.anchor: يجمعونه من غير وجهه ويصرفونه في غير وجهه ولا يتفكرون في العاقبة

TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r17.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r17.claim: “Kalla” rebukes them for failing to do what was commanded concerning orphans and the poor; it may simply prohibit this conduct.
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r17.anchor: وقال مقاتل: معناه لا يفعلون ما أمروا به في اليتيم والمسكين

THALABI:v10p201/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p201/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p201/r1.claim: People love abundant wealth, but that is not how matters should be; when the earth is crushed repeatedly, everything on it is broken.
THALABI:v10p201/r1.anchor: وتحبون المال حبا جما كثيرا يقال جم الماء في الحوض إذا كثر واجتمع

ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r9.claim: Abu Amr and Yaqub read the verbs throughout in the third-person plural: they honor, urge, consume, and love.
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r9.anchor: Ebû Amr ve Ya‘kūb kıraatlerinde de bu fiiller hep yâ ile gāib sîgası üzerine

ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r13.claim: People love wealth intensely and pile it up, forgetting that spendthrift heirs may waste what the hoarder failed to spend for good, leaving the owner only sin.
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r13.anchor: Öyle bir seviş ki {جَمًّۭا} çok, yığmacasına

ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r14.claim: These failures come from neglecting the afterlife and God’s watch; people should use their present opportunity for good, honor orphans, feed the poor, and prepare for the hereafter.
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r14.anchor: Bütün bunlar âhireti düşünmemek, Hak teâlâ’nın mirsâd ile gözetmekte olduğunu hesâba almamaktan neş’et eder

BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r6.claim: They love wealth intensely, greedily hoard it, withhold its rights, and do not use it beneficially; love of wealth is natural, blameworthy when excessive, and may also symbolize corrupt desires of the lower self.
BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r6.anchor: كثيرا مع حرص وشره ومنع حقوق رعدم انتفاع

BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r7.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r7.claim: Some masters interpret the loved wealth as many evil, ego-driven deeds and corrupt states of desire.
BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r7.anchor: وقال بعض اكبار وتحبون مال الأعمال السيئة النفسانية والأحوال القبيحة الهوائية

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428#3/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428#3/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428#3/r6.claim: A report says each person values an heir's wealth more than his own; one's own wealth is only what one consumes, wears out, or gives away.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428#3/r6.anchor: عن سفيان رضي الله عنه في انه قال في قوله : ويحبون المال حبا جما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ' ما منكم من أحد

IBNASHUR:89:20/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:20/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:20/r1.claim: Jamm means plentiful; describing love, an abstract emotion, as plentiful is a metaphor for intense, excessive love.
IBNASHUR:89:20/r1.anchor: فالجمّ مستعار لمعنى القوي الشديد ، أي حبّاً مفرطاً

IBNASHUR:89:20/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:20/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:20/r2.claim: Excessive attachment to wealth is blameworthy because it drives people to acquire it through wrongful means such as seizure, embezzlement, theft, and betrayal of trusts.
IBNASHUR:89:20/r2.anchor: لأن إفراد حبه يوقع في الحِرص على اكتسابه بالوسائل غير الحَق كالغصب والاختلاس والسرقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r2.claim: The majority use second-person verbs to turn from speaking about the human to confronting the offenders; Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb use third person to expose them to the Prophet and believers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : ( لا تكرمون ، ولا تحضون ، وتأكلون ، وتحبون ) بالمثناة الفوقية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r11.claim: Jamm means abundant and intense; the cited verse by Abu Khirash uses it for plentiful forgiveness and illustrates its force.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r11.anchor: والجم: الكثير الشديد، ومنه قول الشاعر [أبو خراش الهذلي]

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p121/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p121/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p121/r1.claim: They love wealth intensely, hoard it, and do not spend it on good.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p121/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى وتحبون المال أي تحبون جمعه حبا جما أي كثير فلا تنفقونه في خير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p399/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p399/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p399/r3.claim: They love wealth intensely; some interpreters add that their love is excessive and shameful.

FARRA:v3p261/r14.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p261/r14.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p261/r14.claim: Hubban jamman means abundant or great love of wealth.
FARRA:v3p261/r14.anchor: وقوله عز وجل: أكلا لما (19) أكلا شديدا «وتحبون المال حبا جما»

JISHUMI:v10p7402/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r11.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r11.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb read the four verbs “honor,” “urge,” “eat,” and “love” in the third person; others address the listeners directly.
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r11.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب الأربعة كلها بالياء

JISHUMI:v10p7403/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7403/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7403/r8.claim: Jamm means large or abundant; the term describes a great volume of water, with a poetic example for abundant water.
JISHUMI:v10p7403/r8.anchor: والجم: الكبير العظيم، يقال لمعظم الماء: جمة الماء

JISHUMI:v10p7405/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r2.claim: The rebuke “rather, you do not honor” answers the claim that restricted provision means God is humiliating people: their own neglect is the fault.
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r2.anchor: لما رد عليهم ظنهم أن التقدير الإهانة، بين أن الإهانة لهذا، لا لما قالوا

JISHUMI:v10p7409/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r5.claim: “You love” censures someone whose desires are confined to worldly possessions.
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r5.anchor: ويدل قوله: وتحبون على ذم من قصر هواه على الدنيا

JISHUMI:v10p7409/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r6.claim: Eating, loving, honoring, and urging are human acts, as shown by the praise and blame attached to them.
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r6.anchor: ويدل أن هذا الأكل والحب والإكرام والحض فعل العبد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754/r7.claim: Hubb jamma is abundant, intense love of money marked by greed and withholding the rights due from it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754/r7.anchor: كثيرا شديدا مع الحرص والشره ومنع الحقوق

MAJAZ:v2p298/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p298/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p298/r1.claim: ḥubban jammā means loving wealth greatly and intensely.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p270#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p270#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p270#2/r7.claim: He interprets loving wealth jamman as loving it abundantly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p270#2/r7.anchor: يعني كثيرا , قاله ابن عباس , والجم الكثير

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p270#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p270#2/r8.speaker: الشاعر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p270#2/r8.claim: The poem uses jamman to mean plentifully.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p270#2/r8.anchor: إن تغفر اللهم تغفر جما … وأي عبد لك

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p270#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p270#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p270#2/r9.claim: He calls the love excessive: people combine lawful wealth with unlawful wealth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p270#2/r9.anchor: تجمعون حلاله إلى حرامه , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p270#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p270#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p270#2/r10.claim: A further possibility is loving money only to stockpile it, using it for neither religious nor worldly benefit, the worst state for a wealthy person.

MUJAHID:v2p757#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p757#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p757#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says jamma means abundant or much.
MUJAHID:v2p757#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ حبا جما ﴾ قال الجم الكثير

MUQATIL:89:15-22/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:89:15-22/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:89:15-22/r6.claim: The phrase means gathering abundant wealth, and it is an expression in the dialect of Mālik b. Kināna.
MUQATIL:89:15-22/r6.anchor: ويجمعون المال جمعا كثيرا، وهي بلغة مالك بن كنانة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p338#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p338#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p338#3/r1.claim: The verbs “love” and “love greatly” are equivalent in sense; the phrase indicates intense, greedy love of wealth and withholding its obligations, with variant readings noted for the surrounding verbs.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p338#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ وتحبون المال ﴾ يقال حبه وأحبه بمعنى ﴿ حبا جما ﴾

QURTUBI-FULL:89:20/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:20/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:20/r9.claim: They love wealth intensely, whether lawfully or unlawfully; jamm means abundant, as in plentiful water gathered in a pool or well.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:20/r9.anchor: { وتحبون المال حبا جما } أي كثيرا، حلاله وحرامه. والجم الكثير

QURTUBI-FULL:89:20/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:20/r10.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:89:20/r10.claim: His verse uses jamm for abundant forgiveness, illustrating its sense of great quantity.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:20/r10.anchor: إن تغفر اللهم تغفر جما وأي عبد لك لا ألما

QUTB-ZILAL:89:20/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:89:20/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:89:20/r1.claim: Overwhelming love of wealth leaves no generosity for people needing care and food; pre-Islamic Meccan greed, usury, and exploitation of orphaned girls show this pattern.
QUTB-ZILAL:89:20/r1.anchor: وكان ضعف اليتامى مغريا بانتهاب أموالهم وبخاصة الإناث منهم

QUTB-ZILAL:89:20/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:89:20/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:89:20/r2.claim: The repeated rebuke and forceful rhythm denounce greed, while the sound of the phrasing depicts its intensity.
QUTB-ZILAL:89:20/r2.anchor: وهو يرسم بجرسه شدة التكالب وعنفه

RAZI:89:20/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:20/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
RAZI:89:20/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr says jamm yajumm means to increase, of wealth or other things; jamm means abundant.
RAZI:89:20/r1.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو جم يجم أي يكثر

RAZI:89:20/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:20/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:89:20/r2.claim: The phrase means an intense, abundant love of wealth, showing that people focus solely on worldly life and turn from the Hereafter.
RAZI:89:20/r2.anchor: والمعنى : ويحبون المال حبا كثيرا شديدا ، فبين أن حرصهم على الدنيا فقط

STUDYQURAN:89:17/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r1.claim: Nay rebukes those who wrongly inferred divine favor or abasement from wealth; neglecting orphans and consuming their inheritance is one example of resulting injustice.
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r1.anchor: Nay is a rebuke to those who make the errors implied in vv. 15–16

STUDYQURAN:89:17/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r2.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r2.claim: These verses may be read in third-person plural instead of second-person plural; either reading is accepted.
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r2.anchor: Some read all of these verses in the third-person plural rather than the second-person plural

STUDYQURAN:89:17/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r3.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r3.claim: Failure to understand God's true honoring and abasing leads people to treat the less privileged inequitably.
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r3.anchor: the implication of vv.17–20 is that failure to appreciate the true nature of God’s honoring and abasing leads people to act inequitably toward those who are less privileged

STUDYQURAN:89:17/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r7.claim: The passage condemns intense love of wealth, as elsewhere in the Quran.

SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r1.claim: Abu Amr reads this and the next three verbs in third person, matching the generic singular human understood collectively.
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو هذا والثلاثة بعده بياء الغيبة حملا على معنى الإنسان المتقدم

SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r2.claim: The remaining readers use second-person forms, addressing generic humanity by a shift in person.
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r2.anchor: والباقون بالتاء في الجميع خطابا للإنسان المراد به الجنس على طريق الالتفات

TAB:89:20/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:20/r1.speaker: author
TAB:89:20/r1.claim: People intensely love accumulating wealth; jamm means abundant or gathered, as water gathers in a pool.
TAB:89:20/r1.anchor: وتحبون جمع المال أيها الناس واقتناءه حبا كثيرا شديدا من قولهم :  قد جمّ الماء في الحوض :  إذا اجتمع

TAB:89:20/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:20/r2.speaker: زهير بن أبي سلمى
TAB:89:20/r2.claim: Zuhayr's line about the water's pooled abundance supplies poetic evidence for the meaning of jamm.
TAB:89:20/r2.anchor: فَلَمّا وَرَدْنَ المَاءَ زُرْقا جِمامُهُ *** وَضَعْنَ عِصِيّ الْحاضِرِ المُتَخَيّمِ

TAB:89:20/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:20/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:89:20/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the phrase as loving wealth intensely and in great quantity.
TAB:89:20/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   في قوله :  وتُحِبّونَ المَالَ حُبّا جَمّا يقول :  شديدا .

TAB:89:20/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:20/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:89:20/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قوله :  حُبّا جَمّا قال :  الجمّ :  الكثير .

TAB:89:20/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:20/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB:89:20/r5.claim: Qatāda also glosses it as intense love.
TAB:89:20/r5.anchor: عن قتادة وتُحِبّونَ المَالَ حُبا جَمّا :  أي حبا شديدا .

TAB:89:20/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:20/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:89:20/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says people love a great quantity of wealth.
TAB:89:20/r6.anchor: سمعت أبا معاذ يقول :  حدثنا عبيد ،   قال :  سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  حُبّا جَمّا :  يحبون كثرة المال .

TAB:89:20/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:20/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:89:20/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets jamm as intense.
TAB:89:20/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله :  وتُحِبّونَ المَالَ حُبّا جَمّا قال :  الجمّ :  الشديد .

TAB-FULL:v24p382/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r1.claim: The people love gathering and acquiring wealth with great intensity; jamm means abundant or gathered together.
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r1.anchor: قولهم: قد جم الماء في الحوض: إذا اجتمع

TAB-FULL:v24p382/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites a verse by Zuhayr about gathered water as linguistic evidence for abundance.

TAB-FULL:v24p382/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the love as intense.
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {وتحبون المال حبا جما} [الفجر: 20] يقول: شديدا

TAB-FULL:v24p382/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r4.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās interprets it as loving plentiful wealth.
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وتحبون المال حبا جما} [الفجر: 20] : فيحبون كثرة المال

TAB-FULL:v24p382/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r5.claim: Mujāhid says jamm means much or abundant.
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {حبا جما} [الفجر: 20] قال: الجم: الكثير

TAB-FULL:v24p382/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r6.claim: Qatāda describes their love of wealth as intense.
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، {وتحبون المال حبا جما} [الفجر: 20] أي: حبا شديدا

TAB-FULL:v24p382/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r7.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says they love abundant wealth.
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r7.anchor: الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {حبا جما} [الفجر: 20] يحبون كثرة المال

TAB-FULL:v24p382/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses jamm as intense.
TAB-FULL:v24p382/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {وتحبون المال حبا جما} [الفجر: 20] قال: الجم: الشديد

TABATABAI:89:17-22/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:17-22/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:17-22/r4.claim: Jamm means abundant and great; the verse explains why they did not urge one another to feed the poor.
TABATABAI:89:17-22/r4.anchor: الجم الكثير العظيم، والآية تفسر عدم تحاضهم على طعام المسكين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p514/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p514/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p514/r1.claim: “Jamm” means abundant; the verb can mean to increase or become plentiful.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p514/r1.anchor: (الجم: الكثير، يقال: جم الشيء يجم جموما،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p514/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p514/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة، الفراء، الكسائي، الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p514/r2.claim: “Love intensely” means loving much and with great force.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p514/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة (¬7)، والفراء (¬8)، والكسائي (¬9)، # (والزجاج (¬1)) (¬2) وأهل التفسير (¬3): "حبا جما":

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p514/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p514/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p514/r4.claim: They avidly gather money without spending it for good, matching their refusal to honor orphans or feed the poor.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p514/r4.anchor: والمعنى: إنهم يولعون بجمع المال، فلا ينفقونه في خير،

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:anmerkung/r1.claim: The whole rebuke also has readings in the third-person plural rather than the second-person plural.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zum gesamten Scheltwort V. 17–20 existieren auch Lesungen in der 3. statt 2. Person Plural

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:20:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:20:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:20:anmerkung/r1.claim: Possessive love is also criticized in 100:8; 76:8 presents it as a possible obstacle to feeding poor people, orphans, and captives.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:20:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Der Vorwurf der Besitzliebe wird bereits in 100:8

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:20:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:20:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:20:anmerkung/r2.claim: Although verse 20's wording seems to condemn possession-love itself, in context it more likely names the motive behind the preceding offenses rather than a separate offense.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:20:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Vor dem Hintergrund von 76:8 ist es aber wahrscheinlicher, dass 89:20 nicht auf derselben Stufe mit 89:17–19 steht

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r1.claim: Verses 17–20 specify the earlier charges against ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Pharaoh: neglecting help for poor people and orphans, metonymically the vulnerable, and excessive love of possessions.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r1.anchor: Wie in anderen frühmekkanischen Texten werden insbesondere die Unterlassung von Hilfeleistungen gegenüber Armen und Waisen

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r2.claim: These motifs also occur in biblical prophetic books and likely belonged to a literary genre familiar to the hearers.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r2.anchor: Es handelt sich dabei um Motive, die auch in den biblischen Prophetenbüchern präsent sind und wohl auch als Elemente eines den Hörern vertrauten literarischen Genres fungiert haben dürften.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r5.claim: Passing life’s test requires gratitude for God’s unearned gifts and patience when they are withheld, plus sharing with the poor and vulnerable and encouraging organized social solidarity; Meccan ethics summarize this as reverence for God’s command and compassion for His creatures.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r5.anchor: bu hususta toplumsal bir duyarlılığın gelişmesine, dayanışma ve yardımlaşmanın kurumsal bir hale gelmesine katkıda bulunmak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r6.claim: The passage sharply criticizes polytheist arrogance, selfish indifference to others, and mad attachment to wealth while teaching Muslims the religious and moral basis for life under God’s will.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r6.anchor: müşrik Araplar’daki Allah’a karşı küstahlık derecesine kadar varan benlik iddiası, “öteki”ne karşı tam bir sorumsuzluk ve ilgisizliğe götüren egoizm ve çılgınca bir mal tutkusu

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r1.claim: These readers use second-person تاء in تحبون, تكرمون, and تأكلون.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the three verbs in third person with ياء, keeping agreement with the generic, plural الإنسان mentioned earlier.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحده بالياء كله .

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r3.claim: A generic plural may be referred to once by grammatical form and elsewhere by its meaning; the passage in al-Aʿrāf illustrates this shift.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r3.anchor: اللفظ، وأخرى على المعنى كقوله: وكم من قرية أهلكناها

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r4.claim: The second-person readings can be understood as an address: tell them this.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r4.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتاء فعلى: قل لهم ذلك.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p370/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p370/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p370/r3.claim: The verbs addressing the audience and their conduct vary between yāʾ and tāʾ; Kūfan readers alone add an alif in تحاضون. The cited rationale for yāʾ is continuation from the preceding context.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p370/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ كلا بل لا تكرمون اليتيم ﴾ ﴿ ولا تحاضون ﴾ و ﴿ يأكلون ﴾

QIRAAT-ER:89:20:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:89:20:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:89:20:2#1/r1.claim: The prefix changes from second-person tu- to third-person yu-, changing the address while retaining the form and object.
QIRAAT-ER:89:20:2#1/r1.anchor: changes the verb prefix from تُـ (tu-, you plural) to يُـ (yu-, they)

ALUSI-FULL:v30p127#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “much” as abundant; al-Alusi cites a line by Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt using the word similarly.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127#3/r1.anchor: وتحبون المال حبا جما أي كثيرا كما قال ابن عباس وأنشد قول أمية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p127#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127#3/r2.claim: Their attachment to wealth is excessive and accompanied by greedy avarice.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127#3/r2.anchor: والمراد أنكم تحبونه مع حرص وضره

BINTSHATI:v2p153/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p153/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p153/r6.claim: These verses connect tyranny and corruption with greed-driven individualism: dishonoring orphans, failing to urge care for the needy, plundering inheritance, and loving wealth until conscience, insight, and the heart are dulled.
BINTSHATI:v2p153/r6.anchor: وبهذا البيان المحكم، ترتبط الآيات التي لفتت ذا حجر إلى مصير الذين طغوا في البلاد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p420/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p420/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p420/r4.claim: Their intense, greedy love of every kind of wealth reveals that worldly calculation dominates them over reason and restraint from desire.

DURR-FULL:v8p509/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p509/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p509/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines *ḥubban jammā* as abundant love, citing Umayya ibn Khalaf’s use of *jammā* for abundance.
DURR-FULL:v8p509/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس إن نافع بن الأزرق سأله عن قوله: {حبا جما} قال: كثيرا

DURR-FULL:v8p509/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p509/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p509/r5.claim: Qatāda glosses inheritance and both “devouring all together” and “intense love” as severe.

DURR-FULL:v8p509/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p509/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p509/r6.claim: Mujāhid says *lamm* means gathering or sweeping things together and *jamm* means much.
DURR-FULL:v8p509/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {أكلا لما} قال: اللم اللف وفي قوله: {حبا جما} قال: الجم الكثير

DURR-FULL:v8p509/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p509/r7.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p509/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan says people consume whatever they find, lawful or unlawful, and love wealth excessively.
DURR-FULL:v8p509/r7.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله: {أكلا لما} قال: من طيب أو خبيث وفي قوله: {حبا جما} قال: فاحشا

DURR-FULL:v8p509/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p509/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p509/r11.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says everyone values an heir’s wealth more than his own; one truly owns only what one consumes, wears out, or gives away.
DURR-FULL:v8p509/r11.anchor: أنه قال في قوله: {وتحبون المال حبا جما} قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ما منكم من أحد إلا ومال وارثه أحب إليه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p573/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p573/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p573/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses jamm as abundant or plentiful and adduces a line by Umayya as evidence.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p573/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: كثيرًا، واستشهد له بقول أمية

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p573/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p573/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p573/r3.claim: The form and root occur only here in the Qur'an; Arabic usage gives jamm the sense of gathered abundance, as in a full measure, abundant collected water, and a mass of hair.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p573/r3.anchor: وحيدة فى القرآن، صيغة ومادة: والعربية تستعمل الجم فى الكثرة مع التجمع

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r1.speaker: ابن فارس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r1.claim: Ibn Fāris explains jamm as abundant, drawing on the sense of things gathering together.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r1.anchor: وتأويلها بالكثير، قاله ابن فارس في (المقاييس: جم)

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r2.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r2.claim: Al-Rāghib links abundance to a pool’s collected, full body of water.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r2.anchor: ومثله عند الراغب مع ربطه باستعماله في جمة الماء، أي معظمه ومجتمعه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r3.speaker: ابن الأثير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r3.claim: Ibn al-Athīr derives jamm ghafīr from gathering and abundance, and ghafīr from covering, yielding a sense of comprehensiveness.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r3.anchor: ابن الأثير فى الجم الغفير: وأصل الكلمة من الجموم والجمة وهو الاجتماع والكثرة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r4.claim: The adjective jammāʾ occurs only with a qualifier and is accusative as a verbal noun, like qāṭibatan and ṭurran.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r4.anchor: ولم تقل العرب: جماء إلا موصوفا، وهو منصوب على المصدر كقاطبة وطرًّا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r5.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reads the phrase as loving the collection and acquisition of wealth with intense love.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r5.anchor: وفي تأويل الطبري: وتحبون جمع المال واقتناءه حبا شديدا، من قولهم: جم الماء في الحوض إذا اجتمع

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī adds greed, rapacity, and withholding people’s due rights to the sense of intense love.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: حبا كثيرا شديدا مع الحرص والشره ومنع الحقوق

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r7.speaker: القرطبي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r7.claim: Al-Qurṭubī allows the loved wealth to be lawful or unlawful; the author finds this apt in light of the next verse’s indiscriminate consumption of inheritance.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p574/r7.anchor: وقيده القرطبى بحلاله وحرامه (الجامع) وسياق الآية يؤنس إليه، مع الآية بعدها

NASHR:v2p399#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p399#2/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p399#2/r9.claim: The Basrans except al-Zubayrī from Rawḥ read the four verbs in third person; the others, including al-Zubayrī, address the audience directly.
NASHR:v2p399#2/r9.anchor: فقرأ البصريان سوى الزبيري عن روح بالغيب في الأربعة، وقرأ الباقون بالخطاب ومعهم الزبيري عن روح

ALUSI:89:18/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:18/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو والحسن ومن معه
ALUSI:89:18/r6.claim: Abū ʿAmr, al-Ḥasan and associated readers use third-person lā yaḥuḍḍūna without an alif after ḥāʾ; the other seven use second-person lā taḥuḍḍūna, and the same person shift applies to the next two verbs.
ALUSI:89:18/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ومن سمعت الحسن ومن معه ولا يحضون بياء الغيبة ولا ألف بعد الحاء

ALUSI:89:20/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:20/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:89:20/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses jammā as much or abundant.
ALUSI:89:20/r1.anchor: أي كثيرا كما قال ابن عباس وأنشد قول أمية

ALUSI:89:20/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:20/r2.speaker: أمية
ALUSI:89:20/r2.claim: Umayya's poetic line uses jammā to mean abundantly, as evidence for the word's sense.

ALUSI:89:20/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:20/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:20/r3.claim: The people love wealth with greed and insatiable avidity.
ALUSI:89:20/r3.anchor: والمراد إنكم تحبونه مع حرص وشره

BAGHAWI:89:17/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:17/r6.speaker: أهل البصرة
BAGHAWI:89:17/r6.claim: Basra reads the four verbs about honoring, urging, eating, and loving in the third person with yāʾ; the other readers use second-person tāʾ.
BAGHAWI:89:17/r6.anchor: قرأ أهل لبصرة :  "  يكرمون ،   ويحضون ،   ويأكلون ،   ويحبون "  بالياء فيهن ،   وقرأ الآخرون بالتاء

BAGHAWI:89:20/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:20/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:89:20/r1.claim: Jamman means abundant: they love accumulating wealth and are passionately attached to it; the idiom جم الماء means water grew plentiful and gathered.
BAGHAWI:89:20/r1.anchor: يعني : تحبون جمع المال ويولعون به

BAYDAWI:89:20/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:20/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:89:20/r1.claim: They love wealth in great measure, with greed and avidity.

BAYDAWI:89:20/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:20/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
BAYDAWI:89:20/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Sahl, and Yaʿqūb read the relevant verbs from “do not honor” through “love” in the third-person masculine; the others use second-person forms.
BAYDAWI:89:20/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وسهل ويعقوب لا يكرمون إلى ويحبون بالياء والباقون بالتاء

BIQAI:89:20/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:20/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:20/r1.claim: The verse makes explicit that their conduct reflects enduring love of wealth, not merely reluctant action under necessity; the object includes wealth of every kind.
BIQAI:89:20/r1.anchor: قد يفعل عن ضرورة مع الكراهة

BIQAI:89:20/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:20/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:20/r2.claim: The verbal noun and its adjective intensify the meaning: their love is abundant, greedy, and rapacious.

BIQAI:89:20/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:20/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:20/r3.claim: Their concern is wholly worldly; they do not turn from wealth toward reason, which restrains whims and desires, and instead turn toward God.
BIQAI:89:20/r3.anchor: ولم يصرفوا أنفسهم عن حبه إلى ما دعا إليه العقل

DURR:89:20/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:20/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:89:20/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses jamm as abundant; he cites Umayya ibn Khalaf's verse using jamm for a great amount as Arabic evidence.
DURR:89:20/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نافع بن الأزرق سأله عن قوله { حباً جمّاً } قال : كثيراً

DURR:89:20/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:20/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:89:20/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses lamman as devouring or consuming intensely and jamm as intense love of wealth.
DURR:89:20/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { أكلاً لمّاً } قال : سفاً وفي قوله : { حبّاً جمّاً } قال : شديداً

DURR:89:20/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:20/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR:89:20/r6.claim: Qatada says turath is inheritance, lamman means severe eating, and jamm means intense love of wealth.
DURR:89:20/r6.anchor: عن قتادة { وتأكلون التراث } قال : الميراث { أكلاً لمّاً } قال : شديداً { ويحبون المال حبّاً جمّاً } قال : شديداً

DURR:89:20/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:20/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:89:20/r7.claim: Mujahid glosses lamman as gathering or heaping together and jamm as abundant.
DURR:89:20/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : { أكلاً لمّاً } قال : اللم اللف

DURR:89:20/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:20/r8.speaker: الحسن
DURR:89:20/r8.claim: Hasan says lamman includes eating what is good or bad, while jamm means excessive love of wealth.
DURR:89:20/r8.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : { أكلاً لمّاً } قال : من طيب أو خبيث وفي قوله : { حبّاً جمّاً } قال : فاحشاً

DURR:89:20/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:20/r12.speaker: النبي
DURR:89:20/r12.claim: Sufyan transmits a Prophetic report: a person's enduring wealth is only what they consumed, wore out, or gave away; the rest belongs to the heir.
DURR:89:20/r12.anchor: عن سفيان رضي الله عنه أنه قال في قوله : { ويحبون المال حبّاً جمّاً } قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR:89:20/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:20/r13.speaker: عاصم
DURR:89:20/r13.claim: Asim reads the clauses with second-person tāʾ in tukrimūn, taḥāḍḍūn (lengthened and unhamzated), and taʾ in turath, with lamman geminated.
DURR:89:20/r13.anchor: عن عاصم رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ { كلا بل لا تكرمون اليتيم } بالتاء ورفع التاء { ولا تحاضون } ممدودة

DURR:89:20/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:20/r14.speaker: النبي
DURR:89:20/r14.claim: Abu Hurayra says the Prophet read all four clauses with yāʾ, in the third-person plural.
DURR:89:20/r14.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أنه سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ { كلا بل لا يكرمون اليتيم

DURR:89:20/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:20/r15.speaker: النبي
DURR:89:20/r15.claim: Ibn Umar likewise reports the Prophet reading the clauses through 'they love wealth' with yāʾ throughout.
DURR:89:20/r15.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنه قال : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ

IBNATIYYA:89:20/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:20/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:89:20/r1.claim: Jamm means abundant or intense; the cited poem uses it of abundant forgiveness, and jamm can also mean a multitude of people.
IBNATIYYA:89:20/r1.anchor: والجم الكثير الشديد ومنه قول الشاعر

IBNKATHIR:89:20/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:20/r2.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR:89:20/r2.claim: Some add that the love is excessive or immoderate.

KASHSHAF:89:17/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:17/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:17/r4.claim: Their conduct also includes loving wealth, hoarding it, and withholding its due rights.
KASHSHAF:89:17/r4.anchor: ويأكلونه أكل الأنعام ،   ويحبونه فيشحون به

KASHSHAF:89:17/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:17/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:17/r5.claim: The verbs here and what follows are read in either third person, “they,” or second person, “you.”

KASHSHAF:89:20/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:20/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:20/r1.claim: Jammā means abundant and intense love, accompanied by greed and avarice and by withholding people's rights.
KASHSHAF:89:20/r1.anchor: كثيرا شديدا مع الحرص والشره ومنع الحقوق

MAWARDI:89:20/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:20/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:89:20/r1.claim: Jamman means much or abundant; a cited line by a poet uses the word in the sense of abundant forgiveness.
MAWARDI:89:20/r1.anchor: أحدهما : يعني كثيراً ،   قاله ابن عباس ،   والجم الكثير ،   قال الشاعر

MAWARDI:89:20/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:20/r2.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI:89:20/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes it to mean an excessive love that gathers lawful and unlawful wealth together.
MAWARDI:89:20/r2.anchor: الثاني : فاحشاً تجمعون حلاله إلى حرامه ،   قاله الحسن

MAWARDI:89:20/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:20/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:89:20/r3.claim: Māwardī also suggests loving wealth so completely that one hoards it and benefits neither religiously nor in worldly life, the worst state for a wealthy person.
MAWARDI:89:20/r3.anchor: أنه يحب المال حب إجمام له واستيفاء فلا ينتفع به في دين ولا دنيا

NASAFI:89:20/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:20/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:20/r1.claim: The verbs habbahu and ahabbahu both mean ‘to love.’

NASAFI:89:20/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:20/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:20/r2.claim: Jamman means abundant and intense love, accompanied by greed and withholding others’ due rights.
NASAFI:89:20/r2.anchor: { حُبّاً جَمّاً } كثيراً شديداً مع الحرص ومنع الحقوق

NASAFI:89:20/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:20/r4.speaker: البصري
NASAFI:89:20/r4.claim: The Basran reading uses third-person forms yukrimun, yahuddun, ya’kulun, and yuhibbun for the corresponding second-person forms in verses 17–20.
NASAFI:89:20/r4.anchor: { يكرمون } { وَلاَ يحضون } { وَيَأْكُلُونَ } { وَّيُحِبُّونَ } بصري

QURTUBI:89:20/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:20/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:20/r1.claim: They love wealth greatly, whether lawful or unlawful; جم means abundant.
QURTUBI:89:20/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : " وتحبون المال حبا جما " أي كثيرا ، حلاله وحرامه . والجم الكثير

QURTUBI:89:20/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:20/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:20/r2.claim: The word describes abundance: something may be called جم or جام; جم الماء when water gathers and increases in a basin.
QURTUBI:89:20/r2.anchor: يقال : جم الشيء يجم جموما ، فهو جم وجام . ومنه جم الماء في الحوض : إذا اجتمع وكثر

QURTUBI:89:20/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:20/r3.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI:89:20/r3.claim: An unnamed poet uses جمّا for plentiful forgiveness, illustrating abundance.
QURTUBI:89:20/r3.anchor: إن تغفر اللهم تغفر جما *** وأي عبد لك لا ألما

QURTUBI:89:20/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:20/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:20/r4.claim: A جمّة is a place where water gathers; a جموم is a well with abundant water and can name water gathering after a well has been drawn from.
QURTUBI:89:20/r4.anchor: والجمة : المكان الذي يجتمع فيه ماؤه . والجموم : البئر الكثيرة الماء
